## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duṭṭhullavācā-sikkhāpada* ("Indecent speech", Bu-Vb Ss 3) is the third training rule of the *Saṅghādisesa* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The disciplinary rule mandates that a monk overcome by lust who speaks to a woman using sexually explicit or indecent language incurs a grave offense requiring formal suspension and rehabilitation by the Saṅgha [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The precept is common to the Vinaya traditions of early Buddhism. SuttaCentral identifies parallels in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as in the Prātimokṣa sūtras and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus documents substantial Pali-internal text reuse with related disciplinary rules, especially *Saṅghādisesa* 2, 1, and 4, the four *Pārājika* rules (Pj 1–4), sections of the *Khandhakas* (Kd 11 and Kd 15), and the *Katāpattivāra* of the *Parivāra* [DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse is likewise identified in exegetical literature, including the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā*, and the *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, alongside cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003) and the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu* [DharmaNexus].
